messages:
ajay: started a quick nsys sweep on the 4xA100 cluster to debug the regression in long tail perf for large batches. tracing cuda+nvtx, attached .qdrep to GCS. saw repeated nvlink peer copy spikes only when host buffers were pageable.

maria: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? curious which memcpy kernel variant is showing up.

ajay: timeline excerpt: 
```
time(ms)  kernel                         stream  bytes
0.0       cudaMemcpyAsync_h2d            s0      1.2M
4.2       nvlinkPeerToPeerMemcpyAsync    s1      8.0M  <-- repeated tail at ~40ms
44.8      nvlinkPeerToPeerMemcpyAsync    s1      2.1M
49.3      kernel_attention                s2      --
```
This pattern repeats for many batches; the big peercopy calls sometimes serialize and create a long tail.

nick: interesting. does the trace show async memcopy merging with prefetch/KV cache work? could be stream scheduling + pageable faulting. any page-fault events in nsys?

ajay: yes, there are vm_faults clustered around the spikes. also we saw a bunch of small prefetch kernels immediately prior to the memcpy spikes (kvcache_prefetch_launcher).

leah: hypothesis: when host buffers are pageable, the runtime issues normal peercopy variant which triggers implicit page migration + fault handlers that serialize the GPU work and kernel selection moves to a safer memcpy path. consequence: nvlink gets saturated and we see tail latency.

maria: good call. try two quick experiments: (1) pin the host buffers with cuMemHostRegister (2) force the memcpy kernel hint (if available) or bump stream priority to separate prefetch.

ajay: ran experiment (1) on a single node: switched to pinned host allocs. repro command: 
```
export ALLOC=host_pinned
python -m bench.run --batch-size 48 --iters 200 --trace out/trace_pinned.qdrep
```
Result: tail went from ~48ms median spikes to ~6ms and overall throughput +18%.

nick: that pretty much confirms pageable stalls. what about kernel selection? did nsys show different kernel name/variant when pinned?

ajay: with pinned allocations the memcpy shows up as cudaMemcpyAsync_P2P_opt (different symbol) and the prefetch launcher calls vanish from the timeline.

leah: action items: 1) add an allocation-mode check in runtime to prefer pinned host buffers for KV cache hot-paths (also provide opt-out). 2) add a quick heuristic: if nvlink peercopy latency > X and vm_faults > Y, automatically try fallback to pinned backing for next N batches. 3) schedule a perfetto end-to-end trace to correlate host page faults with NVLink spikes.

maria: also add a regression test in eng-runtime perf harness that exercises pageable vs pinned for peercopy-heavy workloads so we don't regress.

ajay: created a draft PR with the opt-in pinned path and a small benchmark. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/3124 (WIP). summary of numbers in the run: pageable: p99 peercopy tail 86ms, pinned: p99 12ms, throughput +18%.

infra-bot: nightly-perf job completed for bench/peercopy-sweep, artifacts: gs://redwood-perf/1749923456/

nick: nice. next step for me is to review PR and make sure we don't force pin everywhere (memory pressure). we'll need heuristics and memory accounting.

leah: I'll file a small RFC for the fallback heuristic and attach the nsys traces and perf graphs.

ajay: thanks all — keeping the traces in the perf bucket, will post perfetto link once I have the full end-to-end. :thumbsup:
